items.excerpt: The Odisha government has evacuated nearly 50,000 people to safety as severe cyclonic storm ‘Akvan’ shifts course towards the eastern coast, with landfall likely between Narsapur in Andhra Pradesh and Puri in Odisha. Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi, who chaired a high-level preparedness review meeting, said the state is targeting zero casualties with massive evacuations underway across Ganjam, Gajapati, Kandhamal, Rayagada, Koraput and Malkangiri. With wind speeds expected around 100 kmph and the IMD warning of extremely heavy rainfall across 11 districts on Thursday and Friday, schools have been closed for three days, employee leaves cancelled, and 448 of the 3,000 designated cyclone shelters made operational backed by Rs 20 crore in immediate relief funds.

items.title: The US Fed's next move could be bigger as inflation refuses to retreat, minutes show - The Economic Times
items.excerpt: The US Fed's next move could be bigger as inflation refuses to retreat, minutes show - The Economic Times # The US Fed's next move could be bigger as inflation refuses to retreat, minutes show The US Fed's next move could be bigger as inflation refuses to retreat, minutes show By Reuters Last Updated: Nov 19, 2026, 08:45:00 AM IST Synopsis Federal Reserve officials expressed concerns about rising inflation in their October meeting while keeping interest rates steady. Many policymakers believe additional rate hikes could be necessary if inflation persists and data remains unfavorable. A couple of officials suggested the need for a half-percentage-point increase in future meetings. There is an ongoing debate regarding the pace and extent of rate adjustments as inflation shows no signs of easing. Reuters Federal Reserve officials expressed concerns about rising inflation in their October meeting while keeping interest rates steady Washington: Federal Reserve officials saw a growing risk last month that they might need to intensify their efforts to control inflation, even as they agreed to keep interest rates steady for the moment, the minutes of their October 27-28 meeting showed on Wednesday. "Almost all" policymakers agreed that further rate hikes would be needed if the economy evolved as they expected, the minutes said, while a few said inflation could prove more persistent and require "a shift to a more restrictive policy stance" than currently expected. "A couple" of them went further and argued that the Fed might have to resort to a half-percentage-point increase "if incoming inflation data were unfavorable," a benchmark met in recent releases that showed prices rising faster than anticipated. Among those who supported keeping the policy rate steady in the 3.75%-4.00% range in October, "a few ... indicated that they viewed the decision as a close call," and joined a larger group in urging that the Fed be clear that "the decision to maintain the target range did not reflect a weakening" of the commitment to hit the US central bank's 2% inflation target. At the end of the two-day session, only Fed Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack dissented in favor of lifting the policy rate by a quarter of a percentage point. But the debate highlighted a growing sense at the Fed that inflation will not ease enough on its own for the target to be reached quickly enough. Among those supporting a rate-hike pause, the hope is that coming information will make clearer whether inflation can fall without tighter policy. Prices have been increasing at more than a 3% annual rate, and there has been little improvement in recent months. Last month's meeting also set the stage for a potentially intense debate at the December 8-9 session over the need for a larger rate hike, or at least tougher language about the extent and pace of rate hikes to come, an argument laid out by Fed Governor Christopher Waller in comments to CNBC on Wednesday. The Trump administration has argued that elevated inflation is just temporary and the Fed should ignore it. Inflation has been stronger than expected since the Fed's last meeting, and investors anticipate that the central bank will deliver a quarter-percentage-point rate increase at its meeting next month. ... items.excerpt: Published Nov 19, 2026, 01:15 UTC 4 min read ... - Total CPI inflation was 3.7% and total PCE inflation 3.6% in the 12 months to September. - Core CPI was 2.6% and core PCE 3.1%, a gap of 0.5 percentage point (computed); in August the gap was 0.6 point (computed). - The Fed sets its 2% goal in PCE terms, and its October minutes cite an unusual discrepancy between CPI and PCE inflation. - BLS cannot publish a 12-month CPI change for October 2026 because October 2025 data were not collected. - The next PCE release is due November 25 and the next FOMC meeting is December 8-9. ... The Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) said the consumer price index (CPI) rose 3.7% in the 12 months to September, after 3.4% in the 12 months to August. The Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) said the PCE price index, its measure of prices for personal consumption expenditures, rose 3.6% from a year earlier in September, after 3.4% in August. Excluding food and energy, the picture splits. Core CPI rose 2.6% over the year to September, following 2.4% in August. Core PCE rose 3.1% in September, after 3.0% in August. Subtracting, the core CPI ran 0.5 percentage point below core PCE in September and 0.6 point below in August (computed from the four published rates). Total CPI was 0.1 point above total PCE in September and equal to it in August (computed). ... Energy was the main driver of the headline. The BLS said gasoline rose 9.1% in September and accounted for over half of the monthly increase in the all-items index, and the energy index rose 5.2% on the month and 20.4% over the 12 months to September. ... The minutes of the Fed's October 27-28 meeting, released on November 18, show the staff estimated PCE inflation of 3.6% in September and core PCE of 3.1%, and attributed higher inflation largely to earlier tariff increases, higher energy prices and upward pressure on goods prices tied to the AI buildout.

Why it matters: Fewer than a dozen members voted against Jeffries' nomination for speaker. Raye earned 11 Grammy nominations including nods for song and record of the year for "Husband," and for album of the year for "This Music May Contain Hope." Rosalia racked up nine nominations, days after she dominated the Latin Grammys with her album "Lux."
